{"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=intrinsic+motivation+goal+discovery+autonomous+agents+constraints&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.5220/0012461700003636\", \"title\": [\"Constraints Enabled Autonomous Agent Marketplace: Discovery and Matchmaking\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.5220/0012461700003636\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2024]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.20944/preprints202607.0905.v1\", \"title\": [\"Beyond Human-Designed Objectives: Autonomous Goal Generation in AI Through Intrinsic Motivation and Self-Directed Agency\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Current artificial intelligence systems remain fundamentally constrained by their dependence on human-designed objectives and reward functions, limiting their capacity for genuine autonomy and open-ended development. This paper proposes Autonomous Goal Generation Networks (AGGNs), a theoretical framework for architectures that synthesize, evaluate, and pursue their own objectives through intrinsic motivation. The framework specifies five components: Goal-Generative Networks (GGNs, based on a VAE-style sampler over a goal embedding space), Objective Evaluation Systems (OESs) with six explicit criteria, Intrinsic Motivation Engines (IMEs) implementing curiosity, competence, empowerment, autonomy, and aesthetic drives, Autonomous Agency Controllers (AACs) for concurrent-objective scheduling, and Self-Reflective Goal Refinement (SRGR) for closing the loop. We prove a goal-distribution convergence result (Theorem 1) under stationary feedback and a stability condition for the SRGR loop. The contribution of this paper is theoretical: we identify the structural and motivational ingredients an autonomously-goal-generating agent must possess. No empirical validation is reported. Section VI specifies the protocol — benchmarks (Minecraft-like exploration, creative reasoning, robotic skill acquisition, scientific discovery, multi-agent social tasks), baselines (curiosity-driven exploration, empowerment maximization, novelty search), and metrics (goal diversity, coherence, achievement rate, exploration efficiency) — against which AGGNs should be evaluated.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.20944/preprints202607.0905.v1\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026, 7, 14]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1037/mot0000295.supp\", \"title\": [\"Supplemental Material for Autonomous Versus Controlled Goal Motivation Differentially Predicts Goal Progress and Well-Being Through Emotion Regulation Styles\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1037/mot0000295.supp\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2023]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1007/978-3-319-64816-3_15\", \"title\": [\"Intrinsic Motivation for Truly Autonomous Agents\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-319-64816-3_15\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2018]]}}]", "excerpt_truncated": false, "source_sha256": "8edc1582c2e1ec94a46c01db469b5c3b080801fd6366a12730df688b30fe7683", "verification_required": true, "topic_domain": "unassigned_objectives", "evidence_role": "discovery", "host_tier": "discovery", "source_identity": null, "persistent_identifiers": ["doi:10.5220/0012461700003636", "doi:10.20944/preprints202607.0905.v1", "doi:10.1037/mot0000295.supp", "doi:10.1007/978-3-319-64816-3_15"], "source_candidates": ["https://doi.org/10.5220/0012461700003636", "https://doi.org/10.20944/preprints202607.0905.v1", "https://doi.org/10.1037/mot0000295.supp", "https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-319-64816-3_15"], "source_candidate_identities": {}}
